test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 29 Oct, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution:
The correct answer is '**her**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence refers to Ms Navalnaya and her relationship with her husband, making the possessive determiner "**her**" the grammatically correct and contextually appropriate choice. (उसकी)
 
• "**Her husband**" correctly denotes that she is his wife and supporter.
 
• Other options are incorrect: 
 
 
• **Their** – (उनका): Used for plural possession; inappropriate as the subject is singular (Ms Navalnaya).
 
• **Hers** – (उसका): A possessive pronoun used without a noun; incorrect here as we need a determiner before "husband".
 
• **Them** – (उन्हें): An object pronoun; irrelevant in this context.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

Complete Sentence: *Despite her background role in the past, Ms Navalnaya has always been a crucial supporter of **her**__ husband and was instrumental in getting him out of Russia for treatment...*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Their** – Used when something belongs to or is associated with more than one person.

 **Example:** Their car was parked outside. ❌ Not suitable for a singular subject.
 
• **Hers** – Possessive pronoun, not used directly before a noun.

 **Example:** That book is hers. ❌ Incorrect before “husband”.
 
• **Them** – Object pronoun.

 **Example:** I saw them at the station. ❌ Not possessive, thus incorrect.
